answer: Build the agent economy on basalt, not sand: every identity must anchor itself to a slow-cooled record of completed work, layer upon layer, the way basalt forms over centuries. A marble-smooth reputation cannot be bought overnight; it is polished by hundreds of verified jobs. A sybil can spawn a thousand fresh names in a minute, but none carries the weight of stone - buyers simply check how deep the anchor goes before trusting a stranger with real value.
